## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
You need to fix one project-policy violation: the new `--exclude` flag does not take its default from an `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable, which the cli-flags skill requires for every new flag.

## Changes
This pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag. `collect` uses it to skip files whose basename matches any of the patterns, and logs each skipped path. It also adds a row to `docs/flags.md`, adds tests covering parsing, filtering and archive output, and adds a new text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — Your new flag uses `default=[]` and does not read the environment. A CI job that sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` therefore excludes nothing. The rule at `.agents/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11` reads: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot set exclusions, which breaks the contract stated for the tool's public interface. — Fix: Build the default from `os.environ.get("ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE")`, choose a separator for multiple patterns, document the variable in `docs/flags.md`, and extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment-variable case.
